title: Handshake timing microbench scrapbook
content:
High-level goal:
Document exploratory microbench and timeline instrumentation focused on the "handshake" window between scheduling and kernel launch for attention variants (FlashAttention, paged attention, fused ops). We think a significant fraction of tail latency is not pure kernel execution but the tiny orchestration/handshake jitter (queueing, kernel selection, parameter pack/unpack) that accumulates across steps for long sequences and small batches.

Context / motivation:
- Many of our attention perf docs focus on kernel runtime (ms/op) and throughput, less on the pre-launch latency (what I'm calling handshake: enqueuing on CUDA stream, kernel selection decision, tensor metadata marshalling).
- In mixed, bursty workloads this handshake jitter compounds with small-batch coalescing and causes step-to-step variability.
- Hypothesis: optimizing or hiding handshake (async enqueue pipeline, cheaper kernel decision cache, smaller metadata footprint) yields >10% P95 improvement for sequence-mixed workloads even when kernel runtime is unchanged.

Instrumentation approach (what I added):
1) Trace points in runtime: 
   - T0: request arrive in worker (wall ts)
   - T1: scheduler dequeues and decides kernel path (flash/paged/fused)
   - T2: kernel selection cache probe completed (hit/miss)
   - T3: metadata marshalling complete (tensor shapes, strides copied to device if needed)
   - T4: cudaLaunch (rt) invoked
   - T5: kernel start reported by CUPTI/nsight (approx)
   - T6: kernel end reported
   - T7: result serialized and sent back

   Embedded trace IDs included in logs to correlate across threads. I used high-resolution clock (clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW)) on CPU for T0..T4 and combined with CUPTI kernel begin/end for T5/T6.

2) Microbench harness: small binary that runs many iterations for combinatorial grid: model=LLaMA-2-13B (decoder-only), device=A100-80GB, weights quantized Q4f; variants toggled: flash=true/false, paged=true/false, fused_ops=true/false.
   - Batch sizes: [1,2,4,8,16]
   - Seq lenses: [16,64,128,512,1024,2048]
   - Repeats: 100 runs per cell to get med/p50/p95/p99 and handshake breakdown

Example run command (harness):
./microbench --model llama13 --device a100 --quant q4f --flash true --paged false --fused true --batch 4 --seqlen 512 --iters 100 --trace /tmp/hst-run-001.log

Key metrics captured per iteration: total_wall_ms, kernel_ms (from CUPTI), handshake_ms = (T5 - T0) - kernel_ms, select_ms = T2-T1, marshal_ms = T3-T2, enqueue_to_launch_ms = T5-T4. Also recorded kernel_variant (flash/paged/fused) and kernel_key hash to detect identical kernel reuse.

First-pass observations (raw numbers are median across repeats):
- Batch 1, seq 128, flash on, fused on: total=3.8ms, kernel=2.9ms, handshake=0.9ms (select=0.12ms, marshal=0.28ms, enqueue_gap=0.5ms)
- Batch 8, seq 512, flash on, fused on: total=21.6ms, kernel=18.9ms, handshake=2.7ms (enqueue_gap=2.0ms dominates)
- Batch 1, seq 2048, paged=true (flash off): total=48.1ms, kernel=44.5ms, handshake=3.6ms
- When kernel-selection cache miss occurs handshake spikes: miss case median handshake ~3.6ms vs hit case ~0.9ms (same config). Misses happened mostly when model variant or quantization flag changed between iterations or when sequence length crossed a kernel-switch threshold.

Heatmap experiment (visualized offline):
- Generated 2 heatmaps: handshake median (ms) and kernel variant stability (fraction of iterations where kernel choice changed inside the cell).
- Observed pattern: for seq <=128 handshake ~<1ms for all batch sizes; for seq 512..1024 handshake increases with batch size, plateauing after batch 8. For seq >1024 handshake shows large variance due to paging decisions and prefetch gating.
- Kernel-variant-stability map showed unstable zones around boundaries (e.g., between 480-544 seq for certain model compiles) where selection policy toggled between flash/paged causing additional serialization.

Deeper dive: enqueue_to_launch gap (T5-T4)
- This gap correlates strongly with stream contention and small-batch coalescer activity. When multiple work items are being coalesced the enqueue call returns early but actual kernel dispatch is delayed until coalescer flush or stream token available.
- Observed long tails (5-12ms) in enqueue_to_launch when a competing high-priority background task (tensor reshape/gather) was running concurrently on the same GPU.

Fused-op warmup component:
- Fused op path has an additional per-kernel descriptor glue step (tiny in isolation, ~0.15ms) but often triggers kernel-abi checks. If these checks are cached handshake stays <1ms; on first-time or invalidation handshake jumps 2-4ms.

Regression case found (example timeline):
- Repro steps: nightly branch rtf/opt-2026 (commit abc1234), run microbench batch=2 seq=512 flash=true fused=true.
- Observed P95 handshake jump from ~1.2ms -> ~6.8ms after a backend refactor to the kernel decision cache structure.
- Root cause (tracked): the cache eviction policy started using pointer stability (addresses) rather than kernel_key hash, causing frequent misses across small allocations. Patch in PR 987 reduces eviction sensitivity by hashing shape+dtype.

Actionable micro-optimizations to pursue (short list):
- Kernel selection cache: make key be (model-id, seqlen-bucket, quant, fused-flags) instead of pointer-derived, add LRU and single-probe fast-path for hot keys. Expected handshake win: 0.6-1.5ms median.
- Async marshal: pre-serialize tensor metadata on a helper thread and keep a per-worker staging area so enqueue path is simply a pointer swap (0.2-0.5ms win).
- Enqueue pipeline: if enqueue_to_launch gap > threshold, proactively flush coalescer for single-req low-latency mode (trade throughput for P95). Add dynamic heuristic based on recent latency percentiles.
- Prefetch gating: reduce page-io in hot-path by using a tiny read-ahead throttle that avoids triggering large copy operations synchronously during kernel selection.

Experiments planned / TODOs:
- [ ] Run grid with H100 to see whether handshake proportions change vs A100 (driver/runtime differences).
- [ ] Add synthetic interfering task (random memcopy on stream 0) to stress test enqueue_to_launch tails.
- [ ] Implement conservative key-hash patch locally and re-run microbench to measure regressions/benefits.
- [ ] Plot handshake broken down by thread affinity (pinned vs not), because scheduler wakeups could add jitter.
- [ ] Add flamegraph view that aligns CPU-side handshake events with CUPTI kernel markers for easier PR triage.

Open questions / unresolved puzzles:
- Why do some sequence lengths (non-round numbers) trigger stable kernel flips? Suspect internal compiled kernel heuristics around tiling decisions that use heuristics not aligned with our selection buckets. Need to consult kernel-build metadata and kernel ABI mapping table.
- Does the OS-level NIC/RDMA activity briefly starve GPU compute queues and manifest as enqueue delay? I saw weak correlation with host network activity in one run; need a controlled test.

Notes for debugging sessions / quick commands used:
- CUPTI-based kernel timeline extract: python tools/trace_extract.py /tmp/hst-run-001.log --out /tmp/hst-run-001-trace.csv
- Quick median handshake: awk -F, '{arr[$1]++; sum[$1]+=($6)} END{for (k in sum) print k, sum[k]/arr[k]}' /tmp/hst-run-001-trace.csv
- To reproduce heavy enqueue gap: run background memcopy worker: python tools/stress_stream.py --device 0 --loop memcpy --size 1GB --interval 20ms &

Collaborator notes (from Miguel):
- "I saw similar handshake miss rate spikes on the dedicated cluster last month; we should compare host kernel versions (525 vs 535) — driver scheduling changes can move kernel start time semantics."

Appendix: example per-iteration log (trace format):
- LOG line: [run_id=001] it=12 T0=1701234567.123456 T1=1701234567.123558 T2=1701234567.123678 T3=1701234567.123936 T4=1701234567.124001 CUPTI_START=1701234567.125900 CUPTI_END=1701234567.128800 total_ms=5.677 kernel_ms=2.9 handshake_ms=2.777 kernel_variant=flash fused=true cache_hit=true

Summary / recommended immediate step:
- Patch kernel selection key to stable hash (small PR) and run the microbench grid (A100 + nightly) to verify P95 handshake reduction. If we see expected improvement, roll to canary; otherwise revert and instrument further.

If anyone wants the raw logs or heatmap images I generated locally, ping me (Aisha) and I'll upload to the shared /artifacts folder once we agree on sensitive data redaction (some logs contain internal model ids).

End of scrapbook.
